This separation prevents an unclosed matching transfer or a repeated charge assignment.The geometric extension is also sound. It may contain endpoints of other complete components.1. The previous required revisions are satisfiedPrevious issueRepaired packetAssessmentEven-arm induction used vertices two lattice steps awayThe frozen chamber corner retains  $p_1^c$ , which freezes  $p_2^c$ ; subsequently frozen  $p_{j-2}^c$  retains adjacent  $p_{j-1}^c$ CorrectInheritance of “thin” was unspecifiedThin now means containment in two consecutive rows or columnsHereditary under endpoint deletionSource multiplicity needed clarification $B$  counts distinct complete initial endpoint componentsCorrect indexing for the payment sumFixed-number band obstruction could be read too broadlyThe obstruction is explicitly restricted to fixed prefixes or selections among the defined nonterminal  $B_s$ Correct quantified scopeSharpness paragraph briefly asserted incompatible saturated-band fillingSharpness is asserted only with the sparse forced-support baselineCorrectPhysical boundary containmentThe axial supports ensure the required terminal row existsSufficientFor clarity, the repaired even-arm implications now use actual adjacent vertices:
$$(1,c)\text{ frozen}
\Longrightarrow p_1^c\text{ retained}
\Longrightarrow p_2^c\text{ frozen},$$
and, for even  $j\ge4$ ,
$$p_{j-2}^c\text{ frozen}
\Longrightarrow p_{j-1}^c\text{ retained}
\Longrightarrow p_j^c\text{ frozen}.$$
The prescribed inside support supplies the other occupied neighbor in each step.The same fixed-bundle interpretation applies throughout: “retained” means occupied, possibly as a newly selected vertex. After all source endpoints have been proved unpromotable, no source matching edge can be used, so all source endpoints actually remain in  $P$ .The previously checked all-width/all-depth construction, receiver counts, and saturated-band charge calculations remain valid. In particular, the original corrected whole-source charge is still exactly  $+1$ .2. Complete transverse combs are universally frozen and remain completeWrite a prescribed comb’s endpoints in order as
$$v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_{2a},$$
with actual matching
$$v_1v_2,\ v_3v_4,\ldots,v_{2a-1}v_{2a}.$$
Fix an arbitrary feasible simultaneous promotion bundle. Each end endpoint has its axial and perpendicular selected supports, so neither end can be promoted.Starting at  $v_1$ , the induction is
$$v_{2j-1}\text{ unpromotable}
\Longrightarrow m(v_{2j-1})=v_{2j}\text{ retained}
\Longrightarrow v_{2j+1}\text{ unpromotable}.$$
The last implication uses the perpendicular selected support of  $v_{2j+1}$  and its adjacent retained neighbor  $v_{2j}$ .Starting at  $v_{2a}$  gives the analogous descending wave covering all even indices. These waves exhaust the endpoints because the number of endpoints is even and the actual matching is the prescribed consecutive matching.Thus no matching edge of the comb can be used. Its complete endpoint set, actual matching, and original selected supports all persist.Completeness is preserved for the reason given in the packet: promotion only deletes endpoints elsewhere. It cannot create a new  $P$ -edge or connect previously distinct induced  $P$ -components. A complete component whose vertices all survive consequently remains complete.This argument works for either phase of the alternating supports, every allowed even comb length, and all rotated orientations. It also covers simultaneous bundles involving exterior components.The mouth condition therefore survives normalization. Indeed, every initial endpoint in a mouth belongs to a frozen prescribed crossing comb, so the endpoint set inside each mouth stays exactly the same.3. The exact zero charge of a whole straight comb can be proved directlyThe packet invokes a complete straight-comb theorem. Its precise zero-charge conclusion also follows from the prescribed geometry, so this claim does not require an additional unexamined argument.Consider a vertical comb with  $2a$  endpoints. All its receiver tiles lie in the same physical tile column.A receiver tile containing two endpoints has exactly one perpendicular selected support in its other column: the supports at consecutive endpoints alternate sides. The remaining corner is forced blank by that selected support, which already sees its intended endpoint. Such a tile has
$$(t,p)=(1,2)$$
and raw charge
$$t+\frac p2-2=0.$$
There are two row phases.Endpoints fill whole physical row pairsThe receiver has  $a$  tiles, all of the preceding type. Hence
$$|R_C|=a,\qquad T_{R_C}=a,\qquad |C|=2a,$$
and its whole raw charge is zero.There is a singleton endpoint tile at each endThere are  $a-1$  two-endpoint middle tiles and two end tiles. Each end tile contains its axial selected support.Because the endpoint count is even, the two endpoint perpendicular supports point to opposite sides. Exactly one points into the receiver’s physical tile column. Therefore the two end tiles have
$$(t,p)=(2,1)\quad\text{and}\quad(t,p)=(1,1),$$
with raw charges  $+1/2$  and  $-1/2$ .The unspecified end-tile corners are fixed as well:The axial support forces the other corner in its row blank.When the endpoint’s perpendicular support points outside its tile, the perpendicular support of the next endpoint along the comb forces the remaining corner blank.Consequently an arbitrary feasible completion cannot change these counts. Here
$$|R_C|=a+1,\qquad T_{R_C}=a+2,\qquad |C|=2a,$$
again giving
$$T_{R_C}+\frac{|C|}{2}-2|R_C|=0.$$
Every actual matching edge has both endpoint tiles inside this whole receiver. The granted original matching-transfer corrections therefore cancel internally, yielding
$$\boxed{\rho(R_C)=0}$$
in both phases. Rotation proves the horizontal case.This also explains why whole-comb neutrality does not force neutrality of an individual tile where the comb meets a mouth.4. The weighted shifted-square bound is correctNormalize a mouth as
$$F=\{r,r+1\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\}.$$
The full transverse-contact hypothesis is used in exactly the necessary place: a comb meeting  $F$  occupies both rows in one column. Thus a unit square contained in  $F$  has either no endpoints or a full two-row endpoint column.It cannot have two endpoint columns. Endpoints in adjacent columns would be adjacent in the induced  $P$ -graph. They could not belong to distinct complete components, and their union could not be one prescribed single-column straight component.There are consequently two cases.No endpoints. Three selected corners would give a selected corner two selected neighbors, so  $t\le2$  and
$$\mu\le2.$$
One full endpoint column. Here  $p=2$ . The two corners in the other column cannot both be selected: each would see its horizontal endpoint neighbor and its vertical selected neighbor. Therefore  $t\le1$ , giving
$$\mu=t+\frac p2\le2.$$
The mouth’s first and last columns are still forced completely blank by the long source’s supports. This uses neither endpoint-freeness nor an assumption about the crossing support phases.The shifted squares on column pairs
$$(2,3),(4,5),\ldots,(w-4,w-3)$$
partition all remaining vertices. Hence
$$\boxed{\mu(F)\le 2\frac{w-4}{2}=w-4.}$$
The estimate is uniform over every number, spacing, and support phase of crossings allowed by feasibility. No enumeration is needed.5. Neutral raw-tile removal gives a genuine original-ledger donorThis is the most important accounting step in the extension, and it is valid.Let  $Q$  be a physical mouth tile containing endpoints. It contains one full two-row comb column. At those two consecutive endpoints, the alternating perpendicular supports point to opposite sides. Exactly one therefore lies in the other column of  $Q$ .That selected support already sees its adjacent endpoint, so it forces the remaining corner of that column blank. Thus, exactly,
$$p_Q=2,\qquad t_Q=1,\qquad \mu(Q)=2.$$
Let  $N=(w-2)/2$ , let  $K$  count the endpoint-containing mouth tiles, and let  $Z_F$  be the other physical mouth tiles. The raw counting identity is
$$\mu(F)=2K+\sum_{Q\in Z_F}t_Q.$$
Since  $|Z_F|=N-K$ ,
$$\begin{aligned}
D_F
&:=\sum_{Q\in Z_F}(2-t_Q)\\
&=2(N-K)-\bigl(\mu(F)-2K\bigr)\\
&=2N-\mu(F)\\
&\ge (w-2)-(w-4)=2.
\end{aligned}$$
The conclusion being spent is therefore
$$\boxed{\sum_{Q\in Z_F}(2-t_Q)\ge2.}$$
Every tile in this sum contains no matching endpoint. Under the original ledger it has charge  $t_Q-2$ , with no matching-transfer correction. Thus  $D_F$  is an actual original-ledger deficit.There is no assertion that
$$\rho(F)=\mu(F)-2N.$$
Such an assertion could fail because  $F$  is only a partial region of a comb receiver. The packet correctly avoids it.Nor does the proof remove crossing tiles from their receiver budgets. It subtracts their known raw weight only in an auxiliary counting identity. All their original corrected charges remain in the corresponding whole comb receiver.6. Occupied-mouth disjointness is valid across orientationsFor this part, the weaker mutual exclusions
$$F_H\cap J=\varnothing,\qquad F_J\cap H=\varnothing$$
are sufficient, where  $H,J$  denote distinct complete long-source endpoint components.The contact condition supplies these exclusions: every mouth endpoint belongs to a prescribed complete straight crossing comb, and a long-source component is not such a straight component.Parallel mouthsOverlap puts the mouths in the same physical two-row band.For unequal overlapping intervals of tile columns, an immediately exterior boundary tile of one interval lies in the other interval. That tile contains the first source’s tip endpoint, contradicting the appropriate mutual exclusion.For equal intervals, corresponding tips occupy the same inward-facing column of their boundary tiles. Their row positions coincide or differ by one. They therefore share a vertex or are adjacent, contradicting distinct complete endpoint components.The argument covers opposite-facing sources and rotates to the vertical case.Perpendicular mouthsBecause both mouths are unions of tiles of the same fixed tiling, an intersection includes a whole physical tile. Thus the vertical mouth’s two-column band lies between the horizontal source’s arms, and its row interval includes both  $r$  and  $r+1$ .Writing its tips as  $(u,c)$  and  $(v,c)$ , with  $u<v$ , gives
$$c\in\{1,\ldots,w-2\},\qquad u\le r-1,\qquad v\ge r+2.$$
If  $u\le0$ , then  $(1,c)$  is a chamber endpoint of  $H$  inside  $F_J$ , violating  $F_J\cap H=\varnothing$ . If  $u=1$ , the upper tip belongs to  $H$ , contradicting distinctness.Otherwise the upper tip lies in
$$I=\{2,\ldots,r-1\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\},$$
and the lower tip lies outside it.The outside nearest-neighbor boundary is exactly
$$\partial I=
\bigl(\{1,r\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\}\bigr)
\cup
\bigl(\{2,\ldots,r-1\}\times\{0,w-1\}\bigr).$$
Its top and lateral parts belong to  $H$ . Its bottom part belongs to  $F_H$ .Take a  $P$ -path in  $J$  joining the two tips and inspect its first exit from  $I$ . The exit vertex cannot be on the top or sides, since those vertices belong to the distinct complete component  $H$ . It cannot be on the bottom, since  $F_H\cap J=\varnothing$ .This exhausts all exits. A nearest-neighbor path cannot pass diagonally through a corner.The presence of crossing-comb endpoints on the bottom boundary causes no gap: those endpoints are not vertices of  $J$ . If a proposed  $P$ -path connected them to  $J$ , the purported components would cease to be distinct complete components.Therefore the whole physical mouths, and hence their subsets  $Z_{F_H}$ , are pairwise disjoint.A comb meeting multiple mouths creates no repeated paymentThe same complete comb receiver may meet several disjoint mouths. Nevertheless:Its whole receiver occurs once in the final component sum.Every endpoint-containing tile stays in that receiver.No such tile belongs to any  $Z_{F_H}$ .Different mouths use disjoint no- $P$  tile sets.The repeated raw-weight calculations establish deficits on different donor sets; they do not spend the comb receiver repeatedly.7. The final initial-pair theorem follows from the original ledgerA nonempty promotion bundle strictly decreases the number of matching edges and preserves  $|T|+|M|$ . Hence normalization reaches a terminal pair after finitely many steps.At that terminal pair:All  $B$  prescribed long sources survive unchanged and complete, each with charge  $+1$ .All prescribed crossing combs survive unchanged and complete.Every mouth retains the required transverse-contact pattern.Every other final endpoint component lies in an initial thin or at-most-one-square component.Containment in two consecutive rows or columns survives deletion, and deletion cannot create an all- $P$  square.The granted nonpositive whole-receiver theorem therefore applies to every nonprescribed final receiver. In particular, crossing combs are thin; their exact zero charge is stronger than the sign needed here.Apply terminal tile ownership at this final stage. Receivers are disjoint, and all assigned no- $P$  tiles lie outside them. Section 4 gives disjointness between the assigned no- $P$  sets themselves.With final selected counts  $t_Q$ , define
$$D_H=\sum_{Q\in Z_{F_H}}(2-t_Q)\ge2.$$
The original global ledger first reads
$$\frac{mn}{2}-|T_0|-|M_0|
=
-\sum_{\text{final components }C}\rho(R_C)
+\sum_{Q\in Z}(2-t_Q).$$
Grouping the  $B$  prescribed sources with their disjoint donor sets gives exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{mn}{2}-|T_0|-|M_0|
={}&
\sum_{\mathrm{nonprescribed}\ J}-\rho(R_J)\\
&+\sum_{\mathrm{prescribed}\ H}(D_H-1)\\
&+\sum_{Q\in Z\setminus\bigcup_H Z_{F_H}}(2-t_Q).
\end{aligned}$$
The first sum is nonnegative by the granted receiver theorem. Each middle summand is at least one. Each remaining no- $P$  tile has  $t_Q\le2$ , so the last sum is nonnegative.Thus
$$\boxed{|T_0|+|M_0|\le\frac{mn}{2}-B.}$$
Objective preservation correctly transfers the terminal accounting to the initial pair. There is no initial/final mismatch, unclosed partial receiver, or duplicated physical tile in this deduction.8.
